messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Ramos <olivia.ramos@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Delivery Timeline & Handoff Checklist — Stratus Health Launch

Hi Olivia —

Great to meet yesterday. As discussed, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a compact handoff checklist intended to get us to production in a 10-week window. The spreadsheet includes milestone dates, owners (Redwood vs Stratus), acceptance criteria, and a simple risk column for anything that might delay cutover.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirmation of target go-live week (we proposed week of 2027-09-06).
- Named engineering and procurement contacts for approvals and network/VPC setup.
- Any blackout windows (regulatory audits or product freezes) between now and Sep.

Attachments: Stratus_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1.xlsx (MAP), SOW_Stratus_v2.docx (redline-ready).

Next steps: If that timeline looks feasible, Marissa will own the CS handoff and Monica will lead implementation sprints — I've cc'd both. Can we lock a 30-min checkpoint next Thursday to align on owners and the procurement queue?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Olivia Ramos <olivia.ramos@stratushealth.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Delivery Timeline & Handoff Checklist — Stratus Health Launch

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft MAP and SOW. Quick answers up front: the proposed go-live week (2027-09-06) is acceptable pending procurement timelines — we have a compliance review in mid-August but that shouldn't block a Sept rollout.

Procurement contact: procurement@stratushealth.com (copied). Engineering lead: Olivia Ramos (me) for architecture; I'll nominate our integrations lead after internal sync later today.

Questions/clarifications in the attached MAP:
- Section B (Network & Firewall): can Redwood provide a detailed VPC peering checklist and a suggested CIDR range? Our security team will need to validate against policy.
- Section D (Data Residency): we flagged an optional EU backup replication — we don't need it at go-live but want it scoped as a follow-on.

I can do the 30-min checkpoint on Thu 08 Jul at 10:00 PT. If that works, please send an invite.

Regards,
Olivia Ramos
Director, Engineering | Stratus Health
olivia.ramos@stratushealth.com

Jonas / Monica —

Thanks for sending the MAP. I reviewed the milestone lanes and proposed owners and made inline notes in the spreadsheet (high-level summary below). Key decisions I suggest before the 08 Jul checkpoint:

1) CS Handoff: Marissa (CS) — will own post-go-live success metrics and weekly adoption cadence.
2) Implementation Lead: Monica (Implementation) — will run sprint planning and be day-to-day for cutover.
3) Escalation path: Ben (Solutions Architect) reachable for infra blockers; I recommend a standing "incident channel" in Slack + a weekly risk review.
4) Accept criteria clarification: add an "observability smoke test" milestone under pre-prod that includes end-to-end latency and token-cost sampling (to verify Redwood Optimize knobs).

Risks I'm flagging:
- Procurement: contract redlines in SOW_Stratus_v2.docx may push approval ~2 weeks if legal requests new indemnity language.
- Network: if Stratus requires non-standard CIDR ranges, we may need a short design spike.

Action items before Thu 08 Jul checkpoint:
- Jonas: send calendar invite for 08 Jul 10:00 PT.
- Monica: draft sprint 0 checklist (dev/test accounts, sample prompts, acceptance evals).
- Ben: prepare a condensed runbook PDF with fallback policies and a list of required firewall ports.

I'll join the checkpoint to introduce the CS cadence and acceptance metrics.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Runbook + Milestone Cadence for Stratus Health (attach)

Olivia / team —

Attaching a short runbook and a condensed milestone cadence that maps to the MAP Jonas shared. Highlights:
- Week 1 (Sprint 0): account provisioning, test keys, VPC peering checklist (attached).
- Week 2–5: integration sprints (API mapping, prompt sets, performance baselining).
- Week 6: pre-prod acceptance (observability smoke tests, resource scaling tests).
- Week 8–10: staged cutover and canary traffic ramp.

Attachment: runbook-deployment-2027-06-30.pdf (3 pages) — includes firewall ports, KV cache considerations, and a fallback to the dedicated pool in week-of-go-live if we hit latency regressions.

Olivia — I included the suggested CIDR examples in the runbook and a minimal set of KMS requirements for key rotation. If you want, I can host a short tech-only session after the 08 Jul checkpoint to walk through the VPC template.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
